_what: Every kind of cloud resource the extension creates in a system the SC owns, the call that removes it, and the user-facing path that reaches that call. Property 1 of the root CLAUDE.md (whatever can be done can be undone), made checkable. Enforced by tests/templates/cloud-reversals.test.ts on every jest run. Seeded 2026-11-18 by reading every write the net in cloudReversalsScan.ts finds.
_rules: Every file the write net hits (cloudReversalsScan.ts WRITE_SIGNATURES, webview ui/ code skipped) is claimed exactly once, with its exact hit count: in a resource row's `sites`, or in `notCreates` with why it makes nothing. A new write fails until it is classified; a changed count fails until someone re-reads the file.
A claimed file the net no longer hits is a stale claim and fails. Delete it in the change that moved the write.
A row's `create` must still match in one of its own sites, or the row is a ghost and fails.
A row's `remove` must match somewhere in src/, and must be reachable from every path in `reversedBy` (some file in the path entry's value-import closure contains it).

`projectDelete` sets exactly one of: `removes` (Delete Project reaches the removal, so `reversedBy` must hold `delete-project`), `separately` (the resource outlives a project on purpose and has its own reversal), or `exemption` with a `backlog` id that exists in .rptc/backlog. An exemption whose removal Delete Project already reaches is stale and fails: fix the row.
A row with no `reversedBy` at all must be an exemption.
`exemptionCeiling` counts the exemptions. It only falls.
_method: Static, and it says so. The net finds a write by its call shape, not by tracing data; a write whose verb arrives through a variable and is never written as a literal anywhere in its file would be missed (none found 2026-11-18: every request helper's caller names its verb). Claims are per file with a count, so a second write added to an already-claimed file fails on the count but is not classified by itself. Reachability is import reachability: it proves the removal is loaded on the path, not that the path calls it. It was calibrated on the two known gaps: the Configuration Service delete (EDS-73) and the mesh delete and undeploy (AB-87) are all unreachable from Delete Project, while the repository delete and the DA.live content delete are reachable. A removal pattern names a CALL SITE on the reversal path, not the function's definition: Delete Project's closure loads componentWorkspace.ts, where the integration workspace delete is defined, without calling it.

delete-project.name: Delete Project (and the agent's delete_project), through runProjectDelete

remove-integration.name: an integration's Remove on the dashboard

undo-store-preparation.name: Undo on the demo setup (and the agent's undo_commerce_store_preparation)

agent-aco-admin.name: the agent's delete_aco_access_key, and write_aco_admin with a delete mutation (PL-60)

aco-catalog-rows.what: An ACO datapack's rows in the project's Adobe Commerce Optimizer instance: products, categories, product metadata, price books and prices, loaded through the ingestion API (PL-60). The install record lists each row by the pack's own key.

projectDelete.removes: Delete Project uninstalls the project's datapack through the engine, and an ACO pack's record sends that removal to ACO (removeIfAco).

aco-admin-objects.what: Objects made through ACO's admin GraphQL API: restricted access keys (create_aco_access_key) and, through the agent's write_aco_admin, catalog views, policies and price books (PL-60).

projectDelete.separately: They live in the SC's ACO instance, which outlives any one project. The agent removes each the way it made it: delete_aco_access_key for a key, write_aco_admin with the matching delete mutation (deleteCatalogView, deletePolicy) for the rest.

github-repository.what: The storefront's GitHub repository, from a template, a source repository or a zip. Its files, commits, settings and pushes live inside it and go with it.

projectDelete.removes: performGitHubCleanup deletes the repository when the SC ticks it.

dalive-site.what: The storefront's DA.live content: copied pages, sheets, the block library sheet and account chrome under /source/{org}/{site}/.

projectDelete.removes: tearDownStorefront deletes all of the site's DA.live content.

dalive-site-config.what: DA.live's own config sheet for the site (content.da.live/config/{org}/{site}/) and its permissions.

projectDelete.removes: tearDownStorefront removes the site's permissions, then its config sheet.

config-service-site.what: The AEM Configuration Service site record (PUT /config/{owner}/sites/{repo}.json), with the access grants and admin API keys stored under it.

projectDelete.exemption: No path removes the record: its one delete is inside updateSiteConfig's delete-and-re-register. Delete Project removes the admin API key under it (tearDownStorefront) and leaves the record.

helix-published-pages.what: Pages previewed and published on aem.page and aem.live.

projectDelete.removes: tearDownStorefront unpublishes every page, and Delete Project stops while any is still live (EDS-65).

helix-code.what: The site's code synced to the AEM code bus.

projectDelete.removes: performGitHubCleanup deletes the site's code once the repository is gone.

publish-key-registration.what: The storefront's publish key, registered with the shared prepublish-pdp action so a product added later can publish on first visit.

projectDelete.exemption: Nothing unregisters it. Delete Project deletes the key itself, so the action keeps a dead key for the site, and a site recreated on the same owner/repo name relies on the next registration replacing it.

api-mesh.what: The API Mesh in the project's Adobe workspace.

projectDelete.exemption: Delete Project leaves the mesh deployed in the workspace.

app-builder-app.what: An App Builder integration's deployed app (runtime actions, and what its deploy hooks register).

projectDelete.exemption: Delete Project leaves every integration deployed.

app-management-install.what: An app-management integration's installation through the App Management API: its Commerce association and the event providers its install creates. The I/O Events wire is here because nothing else creates through it (its create methods have no caller), and the provider delete is the agent's one-provider teardown.

projectDelete.exemption: Delete Project leaves the installation in place.

adobe-console-project.what: An Adobe Developer Console project, created in the wizard or by the agent. Its teardown removes its event registrations and providers first.

projectDelete.separately: An Adobe project is picked on its own step and can hold more than one demo, so Delete Project keeps it; Delete Adobe Project removes it.

adobe-console-workspace.what: A Console workspace (the project's own, or an integration's dedicated one), with the runtime namespace, credentials, API subscriptions and extension points that live inside it.

projectDelete.exemption: An integration's dedicated workspace goes with its Remove, not with Delete Project; the project's own workspace goes with Delete Adobe Project.

datapack-data.what: The Commerce records a datapack install makes (Demo Builder's engine: every kind records each object before it creates it), and the demo-data wipe that closes what a demo made.

projectDelete.removes: With Uninstall Datapack ticked, runProjectDelete runs removeDataBeforeDelete first.

datapack-store-pack.what: A pack written into a datapack store (the Data Installer's catalog or Demo Builder's own store).

projectDelete.separately: A pack in a store is the SC's library entry and outlives any one project; the library's Delete removes it.

commerce-store-preparation.what: The demo setup's Commerce changes (AB-77): warehouses and stocks, shared catalogs, ERP attributes, store configuration. Each step records what it made so its undo takes back only that.

projectDelete.exemption: Delete Project does not undo the demo setup; an ERP integration's Remove does (erpSetupTeardown), so it comes with AB-87 when that fix runs each integration's Remove.

erp-integration-data.what: What the ERP integration holds and writes: its records from the ERP fill, its settings, key map and ERP list, and what it wrote into Commerce (owner attribute sets, products).

projectDelete.exemption: Delete Project leaves the ERP's records in its workspace database; the integration's Remove wipes and detaches them first.

core/utils/operationStages.ts.why: A progress label naming the command.

features/ai/server/actionDescriptors.ts.why: Tool descriptions and the commerce_rest_write verb list; the handlers they dispatch to are claimed.

features/app-builder/services/commerceBu.why: The bulk helper's verb parameter type; its callers are claimed.

features/data-installer/services/dataIns.why: The read client's verb parameter type.
batch-get-data-items: a read sent as POST.

features/ai/server/commerceQueryTool.ts.why: A GraphQL read; the tool refuses mutations. The second POST signs in as a buyer for signInAs (generateCustomerToken): a session token that expires, no record made (PL-60).

features/ai/server/acoTools.ts.why: run_aco_query, a GraphQL read of the ACO storefront; it refuses a mutation. The writes go through acoClient.ts and acoAdminClient.ts, claimed above (PL-60).

features/data-installer/services/aco/aco.why: Reads the Commerce backend's GraphQL schema to tell whether the ACO connector is installed (PL-60).
Asks IMS for an access token with the project's client credentials (PL-60); a token expires and makes no record.
The ACO storefront search Clear Demo Data reads to plan; its deletes go through acoClient.ts (PL-60).

features/mesh/services/meshEndpoint.ts.why: A GraphQL query to the deployed mesh.

features/eds/services/helix/helixPublish.why: The admin API's bulk status job: a read sent as POST.

features/app-builder/services/runtimeAct.why: Invokes a deployed web action; what that action writes belongs to its integration's row.

features/eds/services/pdp/pdp404Snippet..why: Browser code written into the storefront; the POST runs in the visitor's browser, not here.

features/ai/server/commerceRestClient.ts.why: The agent's Commerce REST passthrough: the caller names the route, and the same tool sends the DELETE, so the removal travels with the capability.

features/ai/server/commerceRestWriteTool.why: The agent's Commerce REST passthrough: the caller names the route, and the same tool sends the DELETE.
